historical_references.reference: Mark the Evangelist is traditionally considered to be the author of the second Gospel of the New Testament, which bears his name. He is believed to have accompanied Peter to Rome and was responsible for writing down Peter's teachings and experiences in Rome. This Gospel is likely to have been written between AD 50 and AD 70.

In the early medieval period, the name 'Markien' emerged as a female given name, possibly inspired by Saint Mark the Evangelist. It was popular in regions such as Germany and France, particularly during the 12th and 13th centuries.
